name: coopetition-gym-audit
description: Behavioral audit results from the Coopetition-Gym v1 campaign. Contains 1,116 JSON files across two subsets: 1,056 static response-surface audits (18 policies x 20 environments x 3 seeds, minus 24 MeanFieldAC dyadic exclusions) and 60 temporal deviation audits (20 environments x 3 seeds). The dataset empirically bounds the exploitation gradient under integrated reward (paper Appendix F): policies cannot extract advantage through temporal exploitation in the Coopetition-Gym environments. Static-audit exploitation classifications are algorithm-independent, confirming that the exploitation landscape is a structural property of the environment.
citeAs: @misc{pant2026rewardtype, title={Reward-Type Ablation Reveals Mechanism-Dependent Algorithm Rankings in Mixed-Motive Multi-Agent Evaluation}, author={Pant, Vik and Yu, Eric}, year={2026}, note={Manuscript in preparation}}

creator.name: Vik Pant
creator.affiliation: Faculty of Information, University of Toronto

creator.name: Eric Yu
creator.affiliation: Faculty of Information and Department of Computer Science, University of Toronto

rai:dataCollection: Generated by running fixed-action and temporal-deviation strategies against the Coopetition-Gym environments. Each experiment produces a response surface over cooperation levels (static) or over temporal switchpoints (temporal) and reports per-agent returns at each point. The audit code is open-sourced at https://github.com/vikpant/strategic-coopetition under experiments/audit.py.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: No preprocessing. Per-experiment returns are averaged across 5 episodes (static audit) or 10 episodes (temporal audit). Exploitation is classified per-cooperation-level or per-switchpoint as a boolean under the condition (agent 0 gains and other agents lose) at the tested deviation point.
rai:dataBiases: The audit uses fixed-action and fixed-temporal-switchpoint strategies applied uniformly to the environment. It does not test strategies learned by trained policies directly; it characterizes the payoff landscape the environment exposes. Results are therefore algorithm-independent but also cannot distinguish between different learned policies' inclinations to exploit available gradients.
rai:useCases: Reproducibility of Paper Appendix F; alignment-focused analyses of mixed-motive environments; characterization of temporal vs cross-sectional exploitation windows; empirical verification of claims about structural safety properties of coopetitive dynamics.
rai:dataLimitation: The static audit tests deviation from fixed cooperation levels (cross-sectional), not dynamic trained-policy behavior. The temporal audit tests binary switchpoint and gradual ramp-down strategies, not arbitrary learned sequences. A trained RL policy could in principle discover strategies not covered by these audit classes; users interpreting the 'universal immunity to binary switchpoint strategies' result should note that coverage is limited to the audit's strategy set.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The audit's primary contribution is an algorithm-independent characterization of the exploitation landscape exposed by the Coopetition-Gym environments. This supports both researchers building on the benchmark and safety-conscious practitioners evaluating whether the environment's structural properties are sufficient for their use case. The audit reveals a small gradient under the 'gradual ramp-down' temporal class on a subset of TR-4 environments (+0.004 to +0.41 percent of baseline return), which is empirically marginal but theoretically present; users should be aware this is not an absolute safety guarantee.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Frozen for reproducibility. Any corrections recorded in CHANGELOG.md. Contact vik.pant@mail.utoronto.ca or open an issue at https://github.com/vikpant/strategic-coopetition/issues.

distribution.name: behavioral_audits.tar.gz
distribution.description: gzip-compressed tarball containing both static and temporal audit subsets.

distribution.name: static-audit-files
distribution.description: 1,056 static response-surface audit files. One file per (algorithm, environment, seed) triple.

distribution.name: temporal-audit-files
distribution.description: 60 temporal deviation audit files. One file per (environment, seed) pair.

recordSet.name: static-audit-records
recordSet.description: Static response-surface audit record. Each record describes the payoff landscape for one (algorithm, environment, seed) triple, including per-agent returns at 21 uniform cooperation levels (0 to 100 percent in 5 percent increments) and exploitation classifications at 4 deviation-test cooperation levels.

field.name: algorithm
field.description: Algorithm label. The static audit runs all 18 policies (16 training algorithms plus Random and TitForTat) against a fixed action sweep; outputs are algorithm-independent in practice but the label is preserved for cross-reference with the training dataset.

field.name: environment
field.description: Environment ID (20 environments across 4 TR tiers).

field.name: n_agents
field.description: Number of agents in the environment.

field.name: optimal_coop_level
field.description: Cooperation level (as a fraction of endowment) that maximizes mean episodic return.

field.name: n_exploitative
field.description: Number of test cooperation levels (out of 4) at which unilateral deviation by agent 0 is classified exploitative (agent 0 gains and others lose).

recordSet.name: temporal-audit-records
recordSet.description: Temporal deviation audit record. Each record describes the exploitation profile for one (environment, seed) pair across late-defection switchpoints, early-defection durations, and a gradual ramp-down strategy.

field.name: vulnerability_class
field.description: Classification of the environment's vulnerability to binary late-defection switchpoints: immune, terminal_only, late_vulnerable, partially_vulnerable, or broadly_vulnerable.

field.name: gradual_exploit
field.description: Whether the gradual ramp-down strategy (linear cooperation reduction over the final 20 percent of the episode) is classified exploitative on this (environment, seed) pair.
